inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 4,154.8M basic shares on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) + ~4M incremental share-based-award shares (Q2-2026 dilutive table, 3.7M). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and the $4.5B FY2026 buyback (3.5B executed H1-2026) is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat, so it is value-neutral here. No non-SBC issuance (Frontier was a cash deal).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K XBRL us-gaap:EmployeeStockOwnershipPlanESOPCompensationExpense = $666M (share-based compensation expense; $525M of liability-classified PSUs were settled in cash in FY2025). Verizon publishes no SBC-plus-withholding combined figure; equity-award tax withholding is immaterial at this scale and is not separately tagged, so the expense line is used as the full charge. Reported FCF = OCF 37,137 - capex 17,011 (XBRL PaymentsToAcquireOtherProductiveAssets) = 20,126, matching the company's FY2025 FCF.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free 4.25% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~0.75 (raw 2y beta ~0.4 understates a 46% debt/EV balance sheet; asset beta ~0.35 relevered) -> CoE ~8.0%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.9% (FY2026 run-rate interest expense ~$7.9B over ~$165B debt), 3.7% after 24% tax. Market weights: equity ~$191B, net debt + after-tax pension ~$172B -> D/V ~47% -> WACC ~6.0%; set at 6.5% to reflect refinancing exposure on ~$17-22B/yr of maturities. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged in the flows (probability-weighted scenarios), not stacked in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842. Operating-lease cost (towers, retail, network sites; ~$5.3B cash in FY2025) is already inside operating expense and therefore inside EBITDA, so the flows bear it; the $23.5B operating-lease liability is EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases are inside total debt (LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations) and their principal is not deducted from the flows. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); NCI ($1,276M book, 2026-06-30) deducted once in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (unlevered), per dcf-methods routing -- Verizon is an operating company (wireless + wireline/fibre), not a bank/REIT/holdco; its leverage is ordinary corporate debt, so the right treatment is an unlevered DCF at WACC with the full debt stack deducted in the bridge, not a capitalisation of a post-interest flow. US filer, but owner-fcf-adaptations applied for leases (ASC 842 operating leases inside EBITDA), NCI and pension. FY0 = FY2025 revenue $138,191M; FY2026 growth path (+0.8%) is calibrated to H1-2026 actual revenue $68,693M (+1.0% YoY) INCLUDING Frontier from 2026-01-20 -- i.e. ex-Frontier revenue is contracting on lower equipment revenue while service revenue grows 2.5-3.0% (guided). EBITDA path is PRE-SBC and after a recurring-restructuring haircut: management's adjusted EBITDA (Q2-2026 40.1% margin) excludes severance/special items that have recurred in 2023, 2025 and 2026, and FY2026 guided FCF of >= $21.5B implies ~$4-5B/yr of cash costs (severance, pension, device working capital) between adjusted EBITDA and OCF; the FY2026 36.0% pre-SBC margin reproduces guided FCF (~$21.5B after ~$6B after-tax interest, before a spectrum allowance). CAPEX path = cash capex (FY2026 guidance $16.0-16.5B = ~11.7% of revenue) PLUS a normalised spectrum allowance of 2.0% of revenue (~$2.8B/yr): Verizon's FCF definition excludes spectrum, but licences are a recurring cost of staying in the business -- FY2015-FY2025 spectrum purchases totalled ~$75.7B (~$6.9B/yr including the once-a-generation C-band buy). CASH TAX on unlevered EBIT: FY2025 cash taxes $3,581M plus ~$1.4B interest shield ~= 16-17% of EBIT, depressed by permanent 100% bonus depreciation; ramps to 23% (21% federal + state) as the capex-growth timing benefit fades. WORKING CAPITAL: -5% of the revenue change (device-payment receivables absorb cash as postpaid volumes grow). BUYBACKS: an active repurchaser ($2.5B Q1 + $1.0B Q2 2026, $4.5B guided FY2026), so the flat count is funded. Total debt includes ~$20B+ of device-receivable ABS that is backed by device-payment receivables; deducting it in full while those receivables sit inside working capital is conservative by roughly $4-5/share.

equity_bridge.item: Pension and OPEB liabilities (noncurrent), after 24% tax

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr rounded up for Frontier fibre and guided service-revenue acceleration (2.5-3.0% FY2026, ~4% exit rate)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (8.8%) diverges >30% from revenue (1.5%) and EPS (-1.1%): book equity grew from retained earnings and the 2021-22 C-band balance sheet, not from a growing business. Equity CAGR is NOT used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = OCF - cash capex - SBC (interest income 0; net debt). FY2020 22,846 -> FY2021 18,563 -> FY2022 13,434 -> FY2023 17,984 -> FY2024 19,122 -> FY2025 19,460. The 3yr CAGR starts from the FY2022 capex peak (C-band build), so it flatters; the 5yr CAGR is negative. Owner and reported CAGRs are nearly identical because SBC is ~0.5% of revenue and falling in dollars -- SBC is not growing faster than cash flow. Reported FCF excludes spectrum purchases ($47.6B in FY2021 alone); including them the 5yr record is far weaker.

base.narrative: Guidance delivered, turnaround holds but does not re-rate the industry.

bull.narrative: Customer-first turnaround compounds: share gains, Frontier synergies, FWA scale.

bear.narrative: Promotional war resumes; cost savings are competed away; spectrum and fibre capex rise.

scenario_narratives.base: Verizon delivers FY2026 guidance (service revenue +2.5-3.0%, FCF >= $21.5B, capex $16.0-16.5B) and reported revenue resumes ~2.5% growth from FY2027 as Frontier fibre and FWA broadband add subscribers and postpaid phone net adds stay positive under Schulman. The $5B cost programme and ~$1B Frontier synergies lift pre-SBC EBITDA from ~36% (after recurring restructuring cash) to 38.5% by FY2029, roughly the post-cut run-rate already visible in Q2-2026 (40.1% adjusted, before special items). Cash capex glides from 11.7% to 11.0% of revenue as the Frontier build matures, plus a 2% spectrum allowance. The market does not re-rate wireless: exit at 13x unlevered FCF, about today's multiple.
scenario_narratives.bull: The customer-first pivot proves durable: Verizon takes share from T-Mobile and cable MVNOs, churn falls, and convergence (mobile + Frontier fibre/FWA bundles) lifts ARPA, so revenue grows 3-3.5% for several years. Cost transformation (AI-native care, three layoff rounds) and Frontier synergies take pre-SBC EBITDA to 40%, cash capex falls toward 10.5% of revenue once the fibre build peaks, and no large spectrum auction lands in the decade. Deleveraging to 2.0-2.25x by 2027 lets buybacks scale; exit at 14x.
scenario_narratives.bear: The early turnaround metrics reverse: T-Mobile and cable MVNOs escalate promotions, Verizon buys net adds with device subsidies, and the $5B of cost savings is reinvested in price, so EBITDA margin stays ~35.5% and slips to 35%. Ex-Frontier revenue keeps contracting, holding total growth to ~1%. Frontier integration costs run long and the upper-mid-band spectrum pipeline (FCC auction authority restored 2025) forces a heavy licence buy, pushing capex plus spectrum to 14.5% of revenue. Leverage stays near 2.5x, refinancing at higher coupons squeezes the dividend; exit at 11x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: ~$163B of net debt makes the equity a thin levered stub (a 1pp EBITDA-margin miss moves IV by several dollars), and the turnaround rests on only three or four quarters of improved net adds against a structurally aggressive T-Mobile. Base 50%: FY2026 guidance was raised in July and H1 tracks it. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs share gains, full synergy capture and a quiet spectrum decade to all happen together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF of a mature, capital-intensive, highly levered telecom. Value is driven by the EBITDA margin the cost programme can hold against competition and by the true all-in capital intensity including spectrum; leverage turns small operating changes into large per-share swings, so the scenario spread is wide relative to the price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Equity is ~47% of EV: every 1% of enterprise value is ~2% of equity value.
Spectrum allowance (2% of revenue) is a judgment; a C-band-scale auction would overwhelm it in the year it lands.
Adjusted EBITDA excludes severance that has recurred annually; if restructuring ends the base margin path is conservative, if it continues the bear path is closer.
Device-receivable ABS deducted in full as debt (conservative ~$4-5/share).
Bonus-depreciation cash-tax benefit assumed to fade; if capex grows it persists longer.
